_meta.source: Route structures assembled from MOE post secondary admissions pages, polytechnic and ITE course listings, and SkillsFuture work study programme information
_meta.notes: Futures are deliberately stated as wants rather than job titles. Research on adolescent career development, in particular Gottfredson's work on circumscription, shows that teenagers rule out whole fields early on grounds of perceived prestige and gender fit, long before they know anything about them. Naming a job invites that. Naming a want does not. Every future carries at least three structurally different routes, presented in no particular order, because the absence of a ranking is the content.

futures.want: I want to make things people actually use
futures.looksLike: Products, buildings, software, furniture, food, clothes. Something that exists at the end of the week that did not exist at the start.

routes.label: Polytechnic first
steps: Polytechnic diploma in design, engineering or product development
Work in a studio or a firm
Degree later if you want one
routes.note: You are making things from the first semester and you have a portfolio before you are twenty.

routes.label: ITE first
steps: Nitec or Higher Nitec in a making trade
Work, with real tools and real clients
Polytechnic diploma as an upgrader if you want it
routes.note: The fastest route to being genuinely skilled with your hands, and the one employers in the trades take most seriously.

routes.label: Junior College first
steps: A Levels
Degree in engineering, architecture or computing
routes.note: The longest run up before you touch anything, and the widest theoretical base when you get there.

routes.label: Arts route
steps: Portfolio
NAFA or LASALLE diploma
Degree at the University of the Arts Singapore or straight into practice
routes.note: Admission turns on what you have made, not on an aggregate.

thisTerm: Make one thing this month that nobody asked you to make.
Find out whether your school runs Design and Technology or Computing at the level you could take.
Ask your Art or D and T teacher what a portfolio actually looks like.

futures.want: I want to be really good with my hands
futures.looksLike: Aircraft, cars, electrical systems, kitchens, hair, machines, buildings. Work where skill is visible and being good at it is not a matter of opinion.

routes.label: ITE, the direct route
steps: Nitec or Higher Nitec in your trade
Work, often before your friends have finished studying
routes.note: Trained on the equipment the industry actually uses. Employers recruit directly from ITE for exactly this.

routes.label: ITE, then further
steps: Higher Nitec
Polytechnic diploma as an upgrader, GPA 2.5 minimum and guaranteed at 3.5
Technical or work study degree if you want it
routes.note: Each step is a qualification that stands on its own. You can stop at any of them and start again later.

routes.label: Polytechnic engineering
steps: Polytechnic diploma in an engineering field
Industry, or a degree
routes.note: More theory alongside the practical work, and a broader first job market.

routes.label: Work study from the start
steps: A job with an employer
A SkillsFuture Work Study qualification earned alongside it
routes.note: Paid from day one and qualified at the end.

thisTerm: Go to an ITE or polytechnic open house and put your hands on the equipment.
Find one person who does the work you are curious about and ask them what the bad days are like.
Fix something at home that is broken.

futures.want: I want to be there when people are struggling
futures.looksLike: Nursing, social work, teaching, counselling, paramedics, community work, early childhood. Work where the point is another person.

routes.label: Polytechnic health or social sciences
steps: Diploma in nursing, social work or health sciences
Practice, with a degree route open
routes.note: Clinical placements from early on. You are with real patients or real families well before you graduate.

routes.label: ITE first
steps: Nitec or Higher Nitec in health or community care
Work in a care setting
Polytechnic diploma as an upgrader
routes.note: Care sector employers hire from ITE and support upgrading, because the demand is real and growing.

routes.label: Junior College, then a degree
steps: A Levels
Degree in medicine, psychology, social work or education
routes.note: The route to the professions that require a degree to enter at all.

routes.label: Later, as a second career
steps: Work in something else first
Mid career diploma or degree, subsidised up to 90 percent from age 40
routes.note: A very large number of people come into care work in their thirties and forties, and bring something to it that a twenty two year old cannot.

thisTerm: Volunteer somewhere that is not comfortable for you.
Ask a nurse, teacher or social worker you know what they wish someone had told them.
Notice whether you are still interested after the third week.

futures.want: I want to run my own thing
futures.looksLike: A shop, a studio, a service, a business, a stall, a practice. Something with your name on the risk.

routes.label: Learn the trade first
steps: ITE or polytechnic in the field itself
Work for someone else and learn how it really runs
Start your own
routes.note: Almost everyone who runs a good business learned it inside someone else's first.

routes.label: Business and accounts route
steps: Principles of Accounts and business subjects at school
Polytechnic business diploma
Work, then your own
routes.note: Knowing how money moves through a business is the difference between a business and an expensive hobby.

routes.label: Degree route
steps: JC or polytechnic
Business or engineering degree
Industry, then your own
routes.note: Slower to the starting line, wider network when you get there.

routes.label: Start now, small
steps: Sell or make something while still at school
Keep the records
Scale it or learn from it
routes.note: The only route on this list that does not require anyone's permission.

thisTerm: Sell one thing to one person who is not your relative.
Work out what it cost you to make and whether you actually made money.
Find out whether your school offers Principles of Accounts.

futures.want: I want to work out how things work
futures.looksLike: Research, data, software, laboratories, engineering, medicine. Work where the reward is understanding something nobody has explained to you yet.

routes.label: Junior College, then research
steps: A Levels with sciences
Science or engineering degree
Research, industry or postgraduate work
routes.note: The most direct route into research, and the one that asks most of your G3 subjects.

routes.label: Polytechnic applied science
steps: Diploma in applied science, engineering or data
Industry lab work, or a degree with exemptions
routes.note: You are in a real lab in your first year rather than your fourth.

routes.label: Computing route
steps: Computing at school if offered
Polytechnic IT or data diploma, or JC then a degree
Work in a field that did not exist twenty years ago
routes.note: The one field where what you have built counts nearly as much as what you were graded.

routes.label: ITE, then up
steps: Higher Nitec in a technical field
Polytechnic diploma
Degree, often part time while working
routes.note: Longer, and people complete it every year.

thisTerm: Pick one thing you use daily and find out how it actually works.
Build or break something and write down why it did what it did.
Ask your science teacher what they would study if they started again.

futures.want: I want to be in the room where decisions get made
futures.looksLike: Policy, law, management, public service, journalism, community leadership. Work where the job is judgement.

routes.label: Humanities route
steps: History, Geography, Literature or Social Studies at G3
JC, then law, policy or social sciences
routes.note: These subjects teach you to build an argument from evidence that disagrees with itself. That is the actual skill.

routes.label: Polytechnic, then degree
steps: Diploma in business, media or social sciences
Degree with exemptions, often at SUSS or SIT
routes.note: You arrive with practical experience that people who came straight through do not have.

routes.label: Through the work
steps: Any route into an organisation
Take responsibility earlier than is comfortable
Qualifications later, if they are needed
routes.note: A lot of people who run things did not plan to. They were the ones who took the job nobody wanted.

routes.label: Later, deliberately
steps: A first career
Mid career degree or professional qualification
routes.note: The SkillsFuture Level Up Programme exists for exactly this move.

thisTerm: Take a position on something at school and argue it in front of people who disagree.
Read one news story and then find who else reported it differently.
Volunteer for the committee, not the audience.

futures.want: I honestly do not know yet
futures.looksLike: Most people at your age, including the ones who sound certain.

routes.label: Keep the widest set of subjects you can genuinely carry
steps: Choose levels you can sustain
Avoid closing off a whole area you have never tried
routes.note: Not the same as taking everything at the highest level. A combination you are drowning in closes more doors than it opens.

routes.label: Go and try things
steps: Open houses
CCAs outside your usual
One thing a term that you would not have chosen
routes.note: You cannot decide between options you have never encountered. Most fourteen year olds are choosing from a list of about six jobs they have seen on television.

routes.label: Pick a direction, not a destination
steps: Choose the next step only
Reassess with actual information at the end of it
routes.note: You are allowed to decide the next two years without deciding the next forty.

thisTerm: Go to one open house for a route you have already dismissed.
Ask three adults what they actually do all day. Not their job title, their day.
Write down what you were doing the last time you lost track of time.
